chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Ala ibn al-Fudayl —
He said: I asked Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام) about pools in which urination occurs. He said: 'There is no harm, if the color of the water overcomes the color of the urine.'

key_terms.الْحِيَاضِ: pools/basins/cisterns (pl. of حَوْض hawd) — small or large water containers
key_terms.غَلَبَ: overcomes / prevails — the operative legal criterion
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: no harm / no objection — standard jurisprudential formula indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia fiqh ruling on water in a pool or cistern that has been urinated in?
ai.summary: Al-Ala ibn al-Fudayl asked Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) whether pools or cisterns into which someone has urinated remain ritually usable. The Imam issued the ruling that there is no harm (la ba's) provided the color of the water still dominates the color of the urine, establishing visible color change as the operative criterion of ritual impurity for such water — a key principle within the chapter on small bodies of water (al-ma' al-qalil) into which a najasah has fallen.
